nodes.question: What local knowledge institutions and practices were identified for sustainable waste management in the study?
nodes.answer: The practices identified include social cooperation, taboos, local chief's pronouncements, and the conversion of household solid waste into assets.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Botswana is facing significant waste management challenges, including high levels of waste generation and inadequate infra- structure for collection, treatment, and disposal. As a result, landfills continue to be the primary method of waste disposal, often exceeding their capacity and contributing to environmental concerns. Despite the country S laws aimed at enforcing proper waste management, households continue to engage in harmful practices that pose a threat to the environment. This qualitative study, guided by socio-ecological systems framework, explored the role of local knowledge in improving the socio-ecological practice of household solid waste management in Borakalalo ward in Molepolole, Botswana. We collected data through interviews, focus group discussions, observations, and documents and then analyzed them thematically. The following local knowledge institutions and practices were applied for sustainable waste management: social cooperation, taboos, local chief S pronouncements, and the conversion of household solid waste into assets. This study highlights the potential for sustainable waste management through the application of local knowledge and advocates for the integration of local knowledge and the informal sector into the greater waste management planning system.

nodes.paragraph: This theory highlights the social, political and economic factors that influence ecological outcomes. Building on the foundations of social ecology theory, the socio-ecological systems (SES) framework provides a com- prehensive approach for examining waste dynamics within households, between households, and between household solid waste generators and the natural environment. This study explores waste management practices informed by local knowledge that support ecological system sustain- ability. The SES framework helps to identify key variables needed to understand both social and ecological systems, and how they interact with each other (Binder et al. 2013 , p. 15 of 20). By suggesting specific variables, the framework allows us to analyze the potential for sustainable develop- ment within these systems, providing a structured way to assess whether a social-ecological system can remain resil- ient and sustainable over time (Ostrom 2009, p. 420; Leslie et al. 2015, p. 5979). nodes.question: How will this study contribute to waste management solutions?
nodes.answer: The study will add to the inventory of accessible, user-relevant solutions to waste management and will be available in libraries for policymakers and community leaders.
nodes.paragraph: In turn, advertising appeals to the desire for status by promoting consumption, early disposal, and ownership of the latest trends. The desire to appear superior to others, is the basis of social hierarchies. What gets disposed as waste is shaped by monopolistic corporate power: at one end manufactur - ers, marketers and ad men, at the other giant corporations and the notion that garbage is good for business (Rogers 2005, p. 9). Our study focuses attention on the household consumers, who are also household solid waste generators. If households do not yield to advertising messaging about superiority, there will be reduced waste generation and no market for industry goods. Reduced demand for goods defies the capitalist notion of acquisition of wealth as a means to gain power (Bookchin 2007, p. 7 of 12). Tackling this social hierarchy, would be the first step to addressing socio- ecological problems as explained by Bookchin (1993). This study adds to the growing inventory of easily acces- sible, user relevant solutions to waste management. Cop- ies of this research will be available in national and district libraries, providing insights for policymakers and commu- nity leaders to inform new policy directions.

nodes.question: What is the significance of municipalities offering waste education programs in reducing litter on coasts?
nodes.answer: Studies have shown that municipalities offering waste education programs can lead to decreased litter on coasts, as increased citizen knowledge on waste management practices helps in promoting responsible behaviours towards plastics disposal.

nodes.question: What strategy could be effective in influencing Waste Laggards to engage in sustainable behaviours?
nodes.answer: For some individuals in this group, raising awareness, triggering environmental values, and increasing knowledge may be effective in encouraging them towards sustainable behaviours.

nodes.question: How does income level affect engagement in pro-environmental behaviours?
nodes.answer: Older respondents and those with higher income tend to show higher engagement in pro-environmental behaviours, such as waste minimization behaviour, as found in studies (European Commission, 2017; Barr, 2003).
